findings.title: Default proto codec rejects APIv1-only messages
findings.why_it_matters: With this change, every RPC that uses messages generated by gogo/protobuf or protoc-gen-go older than 1.4 fails with "failed to marshal, message is *X, want proto.Message". Those messages only implement Reset/String/ProtoMessage and have no ProtoReflect. The codec now type-asserts against google.golang.org/protobuf/proto.Message (protoreflect.ProtoMessage, which requires ProtoReflect). Before, it asserted against github.com/golang/protobuf/proto.Message (MessageV1), and v1 proto.Marshal wrapped such messages through protoimpl.X.ProtoMessageV2Of. Unmarshal has the same problem at line 49. This is a runtime and API behavior break that the stated pure-migration intent rules out. Converting with protoadapt before calling the v2 API keeps both kinds of message working.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a helper `func messageV2Of(v any) proto.Message { switch v := v.(type) { case protoadapt.MessageV1: return protoadapt.MessageV2Of(v); case protoadapt.MessageV2: return v }; return nil }` and use it in both Marshal and Unmarshal (`vv := messageV2Of(v); if vv == nil { return ...error... }`). Add a codec test that uses an APIv1-only message type.
evidence: encoding/proto/proto.go:41 -- vv, ok := v.(proto.Message)   // proto is now google.golang.org/protobuf/proto
google.golang.org/protobuf proto.Message = protoreflect.ProtoMessage (requires ProtoReflect()); github.com/golang/protobuf proto.Message = protoiface.MessageV1 (Reset/String/ProtoMessage only)

findings.title: Status.Details returns wrapper types for APIv1-only messages
findings.why_it_matters: Callers who read status.FromError(err).Details() and type-assert, e.g. `d.(*mypb.ErrorInfo)`, now fail silently when the detail type is an APIv1-only message (gogo or legacy protoc-gen-go). Those types are registered in the v2 registry through a legacy wrapper. any.UnmarshalNew returns mt.New().Interface(), which for such types is the internal *messageIfaceWrapper and not the user's Go type. The old ptypes.DynamicAny path called ptypes.Empty, which returns proto.MessageV1(mt.New().Interface()) and so unwraps back to the user's concrete type. Status details from gogo-based services become unusable without any error, which changes runtime behavior of the public status API.
findings.suggested_fix: Unwrap before appending: `details = append(details, protoadapt.MessageV1Of(detail))`. MessageV1Of returns the original value for a wrapped MessageV1 and returns generated messages unchanged, since they already implement MessageV1.
evidence: internal/status/status.go:158-163 -- detail, err := any.UnmarshalNew() ... details = append(details, detail)
github.com/golang/protobuf@v1.5.3/ptypes/any.go:77 (previous path via DynamicAny/Empty) -- return proto.MessageV1(mt.New().Interface()), nil
google.golang.org/protobuf@v1.32.0/internal/impl/message_reflect_gen.go:140-144 -- Interface() returns (*messageIfaceWrapper)(m) when the unwrapped value is not a protoreflect.ProtoMessage
status/status.go:45 -- type Status = status.Status (public API exposes this Details())

findings.title: LRS interval error message always reports <nil>
findings.why_it_matters: When a management server sends a missing or invalid load_reporting_interval, the LRS stream fails with "invalid load_reporting_interval: <nil>" and no longer says why. The rewrite discards the CheckValid() error and formats the outer `err` from stream.Recv(), which is always nil on this path because the non-nil case returned earlier. The old code formatted the validation error from ptypes.Duration. Operators debugging control-plane misconfiguration lose the diagnostic.
findings.suggested_fix: `if err := rInterval.CheckValid(); err != nil { return nil, 0, fmt.Errorf("invalid load_reporting_interval: %v", err) }`
evidence: xds/internal/xdsclient/transport/loadreport.go:174-175 -- if rInterval.CheckValid() != nil { return nil, 0, fmt.Errorf("invalid load_reporting_interval: %v", err) }
xds/internal/xdsclient/transport/loadreport.go:165-167 -- resp, err := stream.Recv(); if err != nil { return ... }  (so err is nil at line 175)

findings.title: Conflict resolution downgrades x/tools v0.17.0 to v0.14.0
findings.why_it_matters: vet.sh installs goimports and staticcheck from the versions pinned in test/tools. The base commit (#6939) had just bumped golang.org/x/tools to v0.17.0, and the "resolve conflicts" commit rewrote it to v0.14.0, which is older than even the pre-#6939 v0.15.0. CI's goimports/vet tooling therefore runs an older x/tools than master intended, and x/sys and x/mod pins drift with it. This looks like a merge artifact that is unrelated to the protobuf migration.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore `golang.org/x/tools v0.17.0` (and the matching indirect requirements) from base 5051eeae, keep the new `google.golang.org/protobuf v1.32.0` direct requirement, then run `go mod tidy` in test/tools.
evidence: base 5051eeae test/tools/go.mod -- golang.org/x/tools v0.17.0 (bumped from v0.15.0 by #6939)
provenance: b8374114 resolve conflicts and add changes

residual_risks: Status.Details() error values for unresolvable or empty type URLs changed text (e.g. `message type url "" is invalid` -> protoimpl `invalid empty type URL`, as updated in status/status_test.go); callers that match error strings will see different text.
test/tools go.mod/go.sum consistency could not be verified offline (GOPROXY=off); `go mod tidy` there may still produce a diff in vet.sh.
testing_gaps: No test passes an APIv1-only (non-ProtoReflect) message through encoding/proto codec or through Status.WithDetails/Details round-trip; status_test now asserts `details[i].(protoreflect.ProtoMessage)` and so exercises only v2-generated messages.
